### Start 3 drones (SITL) and connect QGroundControl

- **1) Start the three copters**
  - In PowerShell:
    ```powershell
    cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
    docker compose up -d sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
    ```
  - This launches 3 simulated copters:
    - Drone 1: UDP 14550, SYSID 1
    - Drone 2: UDP 14552, SYSID 2
    - Drone 3: UDP 14554, SYSID 3

- **2) Verify they are running**
  - Show services:
    ```powershell
    docker compose ps
    ```
  - Tail logs if needed:
    ```powershell
    docker compose logs -f sitl-copter
    docker compose logs -f sitl-copter-2
    docker compose logs -f sitl-copter-3
    ```

- **3) Connect QGroundControl**
  - QGC usually autoconnects to `127.0.0.1:14550`. If not, add UDP links:
    - Add link for Drone 1: `127.0.0.1:14550`
    - Add link for Drone 2: `127.0.0.1:14552`
    - Add link for Drone 3: `127.0.0.1:14554`

- **4) Control and monitor**
  - Switch to Fly view to see three vehicles.
  - Upload missions per vehicle if desired (AreaPlanner in Plan view).

- **5) Stop services**
  - Stop all:
    ```powershell
    docker compose down
    ```

- Note: On Windows, `host.docker.internal` is already configured in compose for UDP returns to host, so QGC receives MAVLink on the listed ports.

- Troubleshooting quick checks:
  - Port conflicts: ensure 14550/14552/14554 are free.
  - Logs: use the `docker compose logs -f <service>` commands above.

- Where this comes from:
  - `sitl-demo/README.md` Multi-Drone AUTO Demo section.
  - Fixed compose file `sitl-demo/docker-compose.yml` so `docker compose up` works without duplicate keys.

- Changes made:
  - Removed duplicate `restart` and `networks` keys from `sitl-copter-3` in `sitl-demo/docker-compose.yml`.

- Journal
  - 3-drones start guidance prepared; compose file corrected to resolve duplicate key error.

Do these steps, in order:

1) Start Docker Desktop (ensure it’s running)

2) Ensure Linux engine is active
- From tray: “Switch to Linux containers”
- Or in terminal:
  ```powershell
  docker context ls
  docker context use desktop-linux
  docker version
  ```
  Confirm Server reports linux/amd64.

3) If WSL2 isn’t ready (Windows 10/11)
- Check:
  ```powershell
  wsl --status
  ```
- If needed (Admin PowerShell), then reboot:
  ```powershell
  wsl --install
  ```
- In Docker Desktop: Settings → General → “Use the WSL 2 based engine” (on)
- Settings → Resources → WSL Integration → enable your default distro

4) Pull base image (optional but fast-fail check)
```powershell
docker pull python:3.11-slim
```

5) Start 3 drones
```powershell
cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
docker compose up -d sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
```

6) Connect QGroundControl
- AutoConnect usually picks up 14550
- If needed, add UDP links:
  - 127.0.0.1:14550 (SYSID 1)
  - 127.0.0.1:14552 (SYSID 2)
  - 127.0.0.1:14554 (SYSID 3)

Notes:
- I removed the obsolete `version` line and duplicate keys in `sitl-demo/docker-compose.yml`; compose warning/error is resolved.
- Error “dockerDesktopLinuxEngine pipe not found” means Docker Desktop is not running or not using Linux engine; step 1–3 fixes it.

- Changes made:
  - Cleaned `sitl-demo/docker-compose.yml` (removed duplicate `restart/networks` on `sitl-copter-3`; removed `version:` key).

Do these exactly, then retry the compose:

- Ensure Docker Desktop (Linux engine) is running
  - Start Docker Desktop app
  - In the tray menu: Switch to Linux containers (if you see “Switch to Windows containers…”, you’re already on Linux)
  - Settings → General: “Use the WSL 2 based engine” ON; Settings → Resources → WSL Integration: enable your default distro

- Verify engine/context in PowerShell
  ```powershell
  docker context ls
  docker context use desktop-linux
  docker version   # ensure Server is shown (linux/amd64)
  ```

- Ensure WSL2 is installed and active (Windows)
  ```powershell
  wsl --status
  # If needed (Admin):
  wsl --install
  # Reboot after install, then reopen Docker Desktop
  ```

- Optional: start Docker Desktop service if stopped
  ```powershell
  Get-Service com.docker.service
  Start-Service com.docker.service
  ```

- Pull the base image to confirm connectivity
  ```powershell
  docker pull python:3.11-slim
  ```

- Start the 3 drones
  ```powershell
  cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
  docker compose up -d sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
  ```

- Connect QGC (add UDP links if not auto-connected): 127.0.0.1:14550, 14552, 14554

- If you still see “dockerDesktopLinuxEngine pipe not found”, Docker Desktop isn’t started or is on Windows containers; start it and switch to Linux per above.

- Compose file is already fixed (removed duplicate keys and obsolete version).

  ```powershell
docker context ls
docker context use desktop-linux
docker version
  ```


- Ensure WSL2 is installed and enabled
  ```powershell
wsl --status
# If not installed (Admin):
wsl --install
# Reboot after install
  ```
  In Docker Desktop: Settings → General → “Use the WSL 2 based engine” ON; Settings → Resources → WSL Integration → enable your default distro.

  ```powershell
docker run --rm hello-world
docker pull python:3.11-slim
  ```

- Start the 3 drones
  ```powershell
cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
docker compose up -d sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
  ```

- Connect QGroundControl
  - Add UDP links if not auto-connected: 127.0.0.1:14550, 14552, 14554

- Note: The compose file was already fixed (removed duplicate keys and obsolete version). Your current error is the Docker Desktop Linux engine not running/accessible (pipe not found). The steps above resolve it.

- If still failing, run:
  ```powershell
docker context ls | cat
docker info | cat
  ```
  and check that “Server” exists and “Operating System” shows Docker Desktop with WSL 2 backend.

- Root cause: QGC is listening, but no MAVLink heartbeats are reaching it yet from the containers.

Do this sequence:

1) Rebuild and start the 3 containers (picks up requirements fix)
- PowerShell:
  - cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
  - docker compose down
  - docker compose up -d --build sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
  - docker compose logs -f sitl-copter
  - Wait until you see lines like “Starting SITL simulation…” and “Connect QGroundControl to UDP: 127.0.0.1:14550”. Repeat for -2 and -3 if needed.

2) Ensure containers can resolve the host address
- Check inside a container:
  - docker compose exec sitl-copter python -c "import socket;print(socket.gethostbyname('host.docker.internal'))"
- If that fails, either:
  - Add a Windows hosts allow in compose (extra_hosts) mapping host-gateway; or
  - Temporarily switch env var to `SITL_TX_HOST=host.containers.internal` for all three services and re-up.

3) Open Windows Defender Firewall for UDP 14550–14554
- Admin PowerShell:
  - New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "QGC UDP 14550-14554" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 14550-14554 -Action Allow

4) QGC link setup
- If AutoConnect still errors, add manual UDP links:
  - 127.0.0.1:14550, 127.0.0.1:14552, 127.0.0.1:14554
- Close the error popup, keep the links; as soon as the containers start sending, vehicle(s) appear.

5) Still no data? Quick checks
- docker compose ps (all three “Up”)
- docker compose logs -f sitl-copter | findstr /i heartbeat
- Confirm Docker Desktop is running (Linux engine), and you pulled `python:3.11-slim` successfully:
  - docker run --rm hello-world
  - docker pull python:3.11-slim

Summary
- I removed `docker-compose` from `sitl-demo/scripts/requirements.txt` and cleaned `sitl-demo/docker-compose.yml`. Rebuild, verify containers print “Starting SITL…”, ensure `host.docker.internal` resolves from the container, open firewall for UDP 14550–14554, then add manual UDP links in QGC if AutoConnect still complains.

The MAVLink v1 spec states that `time_usec` can accept timestamps in both microseconds since boot or the Unix epoch. Since it utilizes a 64-bit pack, that seems safe. ---

- Cause: We were sending attitude.time_boot_ms as wall-clock ms; pymavlink expects ms since boot (uint32). That overflowed and crashed.

- Fix applied in `sitl-demo/scripts/simple_sitl.py`:
  - Track monotonic boot origin and send `time_boot_ms = int((time.monotonic() - boot) * 1000)` in `send_attitude`.

- Do this to pick up the change:
  ```powershell
  cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
  docker compose down
  docker compose up -d --build sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
  docker compose logs -f sitl-copter
  ```
  You should no longer see the struct.error, and QGC should start receiving heartbeats.

- If QGC still shows “No Data Available”:
  - Verify containers print “Starting SITL simulation…”
  - Confirm host address in container resolves:
    ```powershell
    docker compose exec sitl-copter python -c "import socket;print(socket.gethostbyname('host.docker.internal'))"
    ```
    If it fails, we can switch env `SITL_TX_HOST` to `host.containers.internal` in compose and re-up.
  - Ensure Windows firewall allows inbound UDP 14550–14554:
    ```powershell
    New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "QGC UDP 14550-14554" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 14550-14554 -Action Allow
    ```
  - Add manual UDP links in QGC for 127.0.0.1:14550, 14552, 14554.

- Changes made:
  - `simple_sitl.py`: correct `time_boot_ms` source to monotonic uptime.
  - Earlier: cleaned compose file and removed `docker-compose` from requirements.

- Cause: pymavlink’s sys_status_send signature changed; we were missing errors_count3/4. Also fixed time_boot_ms earlier.

- Fix applied in `sitl-demo/scripts/simple_sitl.py`:
  - Send full 13-arg `sys_status_send(...)` with sensible dummy values:
    - present/enabled/health bitmasks = 0
    - load=200, voltage=12000, current=0, battery_remaining=100
    - drop_rate_comm=0, errors_comm=0, errors_count1..4=0

- Action:
  ```powershell
  cd D:\WORK\INVERITA\qgroundcontrol\sitl-demo
  docker compose down
  docker compose up -d --build sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
  docker compose logs -f sitl-copter
  ```
  Expect no traceback; QGC should start receiving heartbeats and HUD data.

- If no link in QGC:
  - Ensure host resolution from container:
    ```powershell
    docker compose exec sitl-copter python -c "import socket;print(socket.gethostbyname('host.docker.internal'))"
    ```
    If it fails, set env `SITL_TX_HOST=host.containers.internal` for all three services in `docker-compose.yml`, then up --build.
  - Add manual UDP links in QGC for 127.0.0.1:14550, 14552, 14554.
  - Allow Windows firewall UDP 14550-14554:
    ```powershell
    New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "QGC UDP 14550-14554" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 14550-14554 -Action Allow
    ```

### Connect the 2nd drone in QGroundControl

- Open QGroundControl
- Go to Settings (gear icon) → Comm Links
- Click “Add”
- Type: UDP
- Name: SITL-2
- Listening port: 14552
- Save, then click “Connect” for that link

Repeat with port 14554 for the 3rd drone if needed.

- Vehicles will appear in Fly View; use the vehicle selector to switch between them.

### Short answer
No. The current SITLs in `sitl-demo` are a lightweight Python MAVLink stub (`simple_sitl.py`), not ArduCopter.

### If you need real ArduCopter SITL (recommended for full command/param support)
Use WSL2 Ubuntu (or native Linux):

- Install and run 3 instances:
  ```bash
  sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git python3-pip
  git clone https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot.git
  cd ardupilot
  git submodule update --init --recursive
  Tools/environment_install/install-prereqs-ubuntu.sh -y
  . ~/.profile
  ```

- Start three ArduCopter SITLs (each sends MAVLink to QGC on a different UDP port):
  ```bash
  # Drone 1
  Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 0 --sysid 1 --out=udp:127.0.0.1:14550
  # Drone 2
  Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 1 --sysid 2 --out=udp:127.0.0.1:14552
  # Drone 3
  Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 2 --sysid 3 --out=udp:127.0.0.1:14554
  ```

- In QGC: Settings → Comm Links → add UDP links for 14550, 14552, 14554 and connect.

This gives full ArduPilot behavior (proper COMMAND_ACK, parameters, missions, modes, etc.), avoiding the “did not respond” dialogs you see with the stub.

Yes, you can run ArduCopter SITL in Docker. Use headless mode (no --map/--console) and let QGC be the UI; GUI windows from MAVProxy need an X server and are painful on Windows.

- Headless (recommended)
  1) Clone ArduPilot on host (once):
     - Windows: `git clone https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot.git D:\ardupilot`
  2) Minimal compose for 3 copters:
     ```yaml
     # sitl-ardupilot.yml
     services:
       copter1:
         image: ardupilot/ardupilot-dev:latest
         volumes:
           - "D:\\ardupilot:/src/ardupilot"   # adjust path for your host
         extra_hosts:
           - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
         command: bash -lc "cd /src/ardupilot && . ~/.profile && Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 0 --sysid 1 --out=udp:host.docker.internal:14550 --no-mavproxy"
       copter2:
         image: ardupilot/ardupilot-dev:latest
         volumes:
           - "D:\\ardupilot:/src/ardupilot"
         extra_hosts:
           - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
         command: bash -lc "cd /src/ardupilot && . ~/.profile && Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 1 --sysid 2 --out=udp:host.docker.internal:14552 --no-mavproxy"
       copter3:
         image: ardupilot/ardupilot-dev:latest
         volumes:
           - "D:\\ardupilot:/src/ardupilot"
         extra_hosts:
           - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
         command: bash -lc "cd /src/ardupilot && . ~/.profile && Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 2 --sysid 3 --out=udp:host.docker.internal:14554 --no-mavproxy"
     ```
  3) Run:
     - `docker compose -f sitl-ardupilot.yml up -d`
     - In QGC: add UDP links 14550, 14552, 14554.

- If you insist on --map --console (GUI) in Docker
  - Requires an X server on Windows (VcXsrv/Xming) and allowing TCP.
  - Start X server, then set env in each service:
    - `environment: [DISPLAY=host.docker.internal:0.0, QT_X11_NO_MITSHM=1]`
  - Remove `--no-mavproxy` and append `--map --console`.
  - This is brittle on Docker Desktop; headless + QGC is much simpler.

- Key detail
  - Always use `--out=udp:host.docker.internal:<port>` so SITL can reach QGC on the host from inside the container.

### ArduCopter SITL “Linux setup” but in Docker

- Clone ArduPilot once (host):
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot.git
  ```

- Create `sitl-ardupilot.yml`:
  ```yaml
  services:
    sitl-copter:
      image: ardupilot/ardupilot-dev:latest
      container_name: ap-sitl-1
      working_dir: /src/ardupilot
      volumes:
        - ./ardupilot:/src/ardupilot
      extra_hosts:
        - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
      command: bash -lc "Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 0 --sysid 1 -w --no-mavproxy --out=udp:host.docker.internal:14550"
      restart: unless-stopped

    sitl-copter-2:
      image: ardupilot/ardupilot-dev:latest
      container_name: ap-sitl-2
      working_dir: /src/ardupilot
      volumes:
        - ./ardupilot:/src/ardupilot
      extra_hosts:
        - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
      command: bash -lc "Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 1 --sysid 2 --no-mavproxy --out=udp:host.docker.internal:14552"
      restart: unless-stopped

    sitl-copter-3:
      image: ardupilot/ardupilot-dev:latest
      container_name: ap-sitl-3
      working_dir: /src/ardupilot
      volumes:
        - ./ardupilot:/src/ardupilot
      extra_hosts:
        - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
      command: bash -lc "Tools/autotest/sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -I 2 --sysid 3 --no-mavproxy --out=udp:host.docker.internal:14554"
      restart: unless-stopped
  ```

- Start all three (one line):
  ```bash
  docker compose -f sitl-ardupilot.yml up -d --build sitl-copter sitl-copter-2 sitl-copter-3
  ```

- QGroundControl: add UDP links 14550, 14552, 14554 (or rely on AutoConnect).

Notes:
- This mirrors the “sim_vehicle.py … --map/--console -w” flow from the Linux guide, but runs headless in Docker; QGC is your UI. To use `--map --console`, run an X server on the host and add `environment: [DISPLAY=host.docker.internal:0.0, QT_X11_NO_MITSHM=1]` and append `--map --console` to each command.
- The `-w` (wipe) is used only on the first instance; you can remove it after first run.

Reference: ArduPilot SITL setup and sim_vehicle.py usage [Setting up SITL on Linux](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/setting-up-sitl-on-linux.html).
